prompted_for: A set of choices that is not a card grid (original of concept-q-grid; became LinkGrid: staggered numbered choices joined by one routed line)
composition: six numbered choices staggered in two alternating columns, zig-zag down the sheet
one double-line pipe route snakes between items, left to right and back
small line icon right of each title
header with logo, breadcrumb and arrow
registration crosses at sheet corners and midpoints
mobile: vertical navy rail with dots, numbers left, titles and icons right, arrow at bottom
layout_devices: double-line pipe route with arrowheads linking items in sequence (serpentine)
dot nodes where the route meets each item
big steel-blue mono numerals with slash before title
palette: deep navy titles and mobile rail
steel-blue numerals, nodes and route lines
typography: steel-blue monospace numerals, larger than titles
small regular sans descriptions in sentence case
monospace bracketed view labels and breadcrumb
line_and_texture: 1-1.5 px double-line pipe route with rounded bends
thin single connector lines with dot ends
motion_implied: water travels the pipe route from 01 to 06
each node lights as the flow passes
mobile rail fills as you scroll
t2i_keywords: staggered zig-zag list of numbered items
double-line pipe route snaking between items
desktop and mobile views side by side
t2i_prompt: Flat desktop UI mockup with a narrow mobile view beside it, no device frame, no people. Warm limestone off-white sheet with small registration crosses at the corners and a header of logo, monospace breadcrumb and arrow. Six numbered items of <CONTENT> staggered in a zig-zag across two columns, each with a large steel-blue monospace numeral, a deep navy condensed caps title, a short sentence-case line and a small line icon. One thin double-line pipe route with rounded bends and arrowheads snakes from item to item, meeting each at a dot node. Mobile turns it into a vertical rail with dots.
signature_idea: Choices threaded on one snaking pipe route, so picking a link feels like following the water from stop to stop.
strengths: avoids a card grid while staying very scannable
the pipe route ties navigation to the water-path brand metaphor
light palette with one steel-blue accent is close to the brand
weaknesses: route direction is arbitrary relative to the content order
generic icons (shield clipboard, funnel) feel stock
some lines crossing between items read as clutter
stainless and SCADA copy is off-offer (ignore)
brand_fit_why: Navy on limestone with one steel-blue accent, mono numerals, thin precise lines and air fit well; condensed caps titles and stock icons are the only drift.
